business_problem: The Bank of Canada needed to modernize central banking operations on Azure while simultaneously building internal cloud, DevOps, and data skills so staff could operate the new environment effectively.
solution_summary: The Bank of Canada paired a long-horizon Azure migration with Microsoft Learn-based workforce upskilling so cloud transformation did not outpace staff capability. Its IT organization established a Cloud Centre of Excellence, moved toward a hybrid services-oriented environment on Microsoft Azure, and built agile DevOps delivery around cloud development resources such as Azure Data Lake and a cloud-first ERP solution for HR. In parallel, the bank embedded Microsoft Learn content into its internal learning experience platform so teams could follow targeted journeys from fundamentals through certification as workloads and operating models changed. This created a repeatable loop in which requirements, development, deployment, training, and operations reinforce one another, letting the bank build internal cloud expertise instead of relying only on external talent while supporting hybrid work and continuous delivery.

solution_components.role: Provides the cloud foundation for the bank’s hybrid services-oriented target architecture.

solution_components.name: Azure Data Lake
solution_components.role: Supports cloud-based development resources and emerging data-driven initiatives.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Learn
solution_components.role: Supplies targeted training content through the bank’s internal learning experience platform.

data_flow: Requirements move into Azure-based development and deployment cycles, while Microsoft Learn content feeds role-specific learning journeys that prepare staff to build, run, and continuously improve the new cloud environment.
business_outcome: The bank accelerated Azure adoption, supported hybrid-work continuity, and created an internal cloud-skills engine that helps teams deliver continuous value instead of treating transformation as a one-off migration.
